 Catamounts, Bulldogs Ride Streaks into Saturday’s SoCon Showdown
 Western Carolina seeks its fourth-straight series win Saturday in Birmingham
 Story Links
 Western Carolina at Samford - Watch ESPN 
 Western Carolina at Samford - Listen to CSN 
 Western Carolina at Samford - Live Stats 
 Cullowhee, N.C. – Western Carolina football looks to keep a pair of streaks alive Saturday afternoon in Birmingham as two of the Southern Conference's hottest teams meet at Pete Hanna Stadium.
Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET / 2:30 p.m. CT, as WCU visits Samford in league action.
The Catamounts carry a two-game winning streak into Saturday's SoCon showdown, and have won three straight against Samford heading into the teams' 24th all-time series meeting. The Bulldogs have won three straight SoCon contests, the third-longest active win streak in the conference.
WCU's recent victories include a 27-26 road win at Furman on Oct. 31, followed by last week's dominant 26-10 home win over Wofford. Samford has pieced together three consecutive victories, including a dramatic 37-35 upset of No. 19 ETSU last Saturday in Johnson City, Tenn., and a 10-9, come-from-behind walk-off win over Wofford in its lone home win during the current win streak. In fact, Samford's last two victories both came on the final possession of the game.
Entering its penultimate regular-season game, Western Carolina returns to the site of a thrilling 47-42 victory in 2024. That win marked the Catamounts' first triumph at Samford since 1969 and snapped a 10-game road slide against the Bulldogs.
Saturday's game will be streamed on ESPN+ ( paid subscription required ), with live audio from the Catamount Sports Network on four stations and seven frequencies across western North Carolina and online at CatamountSports.com . Fans can also follow with live stats online .
 Game 9: Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026  •  3:30 p.m. ET / 2:30 p.m. CT
 Location: Birmingham, Ala. (Pete Hanna Stadium)

 Strength-on-Strength – Red-Zone Numbers in 2026: 
Western Carolina enters the weekend as the Southern Conference's best team in the red zone, by percentage. The Catamounts have scored on 35-of-38 trips inside the 20-yard line, boasting a 92.1% success rate, ranking seventh in the NCAA FCS. The Catamounts have 23 touchdowns and 12 field goals.
Samford leads the SoCon in red zone defense, limiting foes to a 77.4% success rate, allowing 24 scores on 31 trips. Teams have 14 touchdowns and are 10-of-11 on field goals after trips inside the 20-yard line. The Bulldogs rank 33rd in the NCAA FCS.
 Inside the Numbers – Catamounts vs. Bulldogs: 
 Western Carolina enters the weekend averaging 10 more points per game than Samford, 29.2 to 19.0 on offense, with WCU ranked third in the SoCon in scoring offense … Defensively, the Bulldogs are surrendering just 22.9 points per game, seven better than WCU at 29.7 per game;
 The Catamounts boast the SoCon's third-best offense this season, averaging 394.3 yards per game, while Samford is eighth at 297.1 … Samford's defense is fifth in the league, limiting teams to 345.3 yards per game, while WCU has allowed 419.1 yards per contest, including an FBS opponent with the Bulldogs visiting Auburn next week;
 Saturday's matchup features two of the SoCon's most productive passing attacks  – WCU is second with an average of 250.6 yards through the air per game, while Samford is fourth at 213.2 yards per contest;
 Samford ranks last in the SoCon in rushing, averaging just 83.9 yards per game, while WCU has moved to fifth with 143.7 rushing yards per game;
 Western Carolina leads the SoCon with 29 sacks, while Samford has surrendered that same number, ninth out of 10 teams in the conference .. the Catamount defense also has 10 interceptions collectively, tied for the second-most in the SoCon;
 Catamount quarterback Lex Thomas LEADS the Southern Conference in total offense, averaging 273.5 yards per game, which includes the second-most passing yards per game at 239.1;
 Three of the top seven receivers in the SoCon will share the field on Saturday – WCU's AJ Colombo is fifth with 53.7 yards per game, and is second in the league with 47 receptions … Teammate Jai Boyd averages 46.6 yards per game, seventh overall, and has a team-best five receiving touchdowns … Samford's Marquise Henderson is fourth in the conference with 54.4 receiving yards per game this season, with three scores;
 WCU kicker Bryan McCollum is tied for the SoCon lead with 80 points scored, averaging 8.0 per game;
 Western Carolina was picked FOURTH in the preseason poll, while Samford was picked eighth in the 10-team league by the head coaches.
 Western Carolina vs. Samford – All-Time Series: 
Saturday marks the 24th all-time meeting between Western Carolina and Samford. While the Bulldogs hold a 17-6 series advantage, the Catamounts enter having won three straight against Samford, their longest streak in the series. WCU trails in games played in Birmingham, 2-10, snapping a 10-game series slide with a 47-42 victory on the road back in 2024.
Scoring and yardage have come in bunches over the past three meetings, with both teams averaging over 500 yards of total offense – WCU 587 yards (417 passing, 170 rushing) and Samford at 501 yards (324 passing, 177 rushing). The Catamounts have outscored the Bulldogs 127-to-84 in the current streak, averaging 42.3 points per game against 28.
Before WCU's three-straight wins, Samford won five in a row over the Catamounts. The last Bulldog win came on Sept. 24, 2022, in Birmingham.
 Up Next for Western Carolina: 
The Catamounts return to E.J. Whitmire Stadium / Bob Waters Field to close the 2026 regular season next Saturday, Nov. 21, hosting The Citadel with a 1 p.m. kickoff. All fans are encouraged to wear purple to the game as the Catamounts will dress in all purple for the home finale.
WCU will honor its 2026 Senior Class, including football, cheerleaders, dance team, and "Pride of the Mountains" Marching Band, as part of Senior Day festivities. Saturday is also Hall of Fame Day, as WCU enshrines its latest class, including the school's inaugural fast-pitch softball team from 2006, former MLB standout Greg Holland (2005-07), record-setting football defensive end Michale Spicer (2000-03), and longtime South Point High coach Phil Tate (1963-66).
